Word order in a typological sample

Source: R/data.R
word_order.Rd

400 invented languages from 100 invented families in six invented areas. Languages mostly inherit their family's word order, so languages from the same family are similar. Adposition order and case marking correlate with word order, in the spirit of Greenberg's universals. Family sizes are skewed: a few large families and many small ones.

Usage

word_order

Format

A tibble with 400 rows and 8 columns:

language

Language ID, L001 to L400.

family

"Family 001" to "Family 100".

area

"Area A" to "Area F".

order

Basic word order: "SOV", "SVO", "VSO" or "no dominant order".

adpositions

"postpositions" or "prepositions".

case_marking

Whether nouns are case-marked, "no" or "yes".

consonants

Size of the consonant inventory.

vowels

Size of the vowel inventory.

Source

data-raw/word_order.R

Details

True model: each family draws a word order from its area's preferences; each language keeps it with probability 0.8 and otherwise draws again. Postpositions have probability 0.92 in SOV, 0.5 in no-dominant-order and 0.12 in VO languages. Case marking has probability 0.7 in SOV and 0.3 in other languages. Consonant inventories are 6 plus a negative binomial count (mean 16, by-family variation); vowel inventories are 3 plus a Poisson count (mean 2.5). Overall, about 44% of the languages are SOV, 36% SVO, 6% VSO and 14% have no dominant order, close to the world-wide proportions in WALS (feature 81A). All language, family and area names and all figures are invented.

References

Dryer, M. S. (2013). Order of subject, object and verb. In M. S. Dryer & M. Haspelmath (eds.), WALS Online. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://wals.info/chapter/81

Greenberg, J. H. (1963). Some universals of grammar with particular reference to the order of meaningful elements. In J. H. Greenberg (ed.), Universals of Language (pp. 58-90). Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.

Examples

table(word_order$order, word_order$adpositions)
#>                    
#>                     postpositions prepositions
#>   SOV                         158           17
#>   SVO                          20          125
#>   VSO                           1           23
#>   no dominant order            26           30
